practiceSentences: The journal publishes academic writing about art.
What academic evidence supports this reading?
Academic writing states its sources for everything.
She took an academic approach to a popular subject.
Academic also means of no practical importance, which is a different use.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: Made of a hard grey building material, or describing something solid and definite.
practiceSentences: They planned a wide circular concrete platform for the new turbine.
Is the storehouse floor made of concrete or old wooden planks?
Amara, the concrete path is finally strong enough to walk on!
The proposal gave concrete reasons for protecting the remaining forest.
A concrete example beats an abstract argument every time.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: Settling something firmly, or able to decide quickly.
practiceSentences: The final scene is decisive; everything before it is preparation.
What was the decisive argument?
A decisive moment leaves nothing still open.
She was decisive under pressure and calm afterwards.
Decisive settles the matter; divisive splits it.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: Clear and easy to see or understand.
practiceSentences: Her skill is evident in every brushstroke.
Is the artist's intention evident from the title?
What is evident to one viewer may be invisible to another.
The influence of the earlier painter is evident throughout.
Evident means plain to see; evidence is what makes it so.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: Not taking sides; treating everyone equally and fairly.
practiceSentences: The impartial judges tasted all forty dishes before quietly comparing their scores backstage.
Can a judge stay impartial when her own niece is performing in the final round?
"I must remain impartial," said the referee, "even though both teams come from my street."
I respect impartial decisions even when they go against my friends, because fairness protects everyone.
"We must be impartial," she reminded them.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: Not suitable for the situation or the audience.
practiceSentences: The music was inappropriate for such a quiet scene.
Why is that word inappropriate in a formal review?
Inappropriate depends entirely on the occasion.
She judged the image inappropriate for a younger audience.
Inappropriate means wrong for here, not wrong in itself.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: In the middle, between two stages or levels.
practiceSentences: The class is intermediate, between beginner and advanced.
Which intermediate step did she leave out?
An intermediate colour sits between two on the wheel.
The sketch is an intermediate stage, not the finished work.
Intermediate is a position, not a judgement.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: Coming before the main part, in preparation for it.
practiceSentences: The preliminary sketches show how the idea changed.
What preliminary work does this need?
A preliminary result may be overturned by the full study.
She held a preliminary meeting before writing anything.
Preliminary comes first and is not meant to be final.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: Very great in size, amount, or force.
practiceSentences: What a tremendous storm that was last night!
Sami showed tremendous courage when he rescued the kitten.
Building the new bridge required a tremendous amount of effort.
Wasn't the noise from the concert absolutely tremendous?
Tremendous once meant frightening, and still carries some of that.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: A strong feeling of caring about someone else's suffering and wanting to help them.
practiceSentences: Amara showed great compassion when she comforted her upset friend.
Why is compassion just as important as fairness, Nora?
Well done, Amal, for treating everyone with such compassion!
The whole school was encouraged to act with compassion and kindness.
Compassion notices the suffering and then does something about it.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: To do with what is morally right and fair.
practiceSentences: An ethical photographer asks before taking the picture.
Is it ethical to edit a documentary this heavily?
An ethical choice may cost you the better story.
The gallery published its ethical guidelines.
Ethical asks what is right; legal asks what is allowed.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: Making sure everyone is welcomed and able to take part.
practiceSentences: The festival's inclusion of local artists changed its character.
What does inclusion look like in a school choir?
Inclusion is more than an open door.
Her work on inclusion brought new audiences to the gallery.
Inclusion means taking part, not merely being allowed in.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: Saying what you need or think clearly and without aggression.
practiceSentences: Assertiveness is saying no without an apology.
How is assertiveness different from rudeness?
Assertiveness states a need; aggression makes a demand.
She answered with quiet assertiveness and the room listened.
Assertiveness can be learned, which is why it is taught.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: The process of choosing between possible courses of action.
practiceSentences: Good decision-making needs information and a deadline.
Who is responsible for decision-making here?
Decision-making improves when the options are written down.
The group's decision-making slowed as it grew.
Decision-making is a skill, not a personality.

words.group: Words: the arts, and the effect words have
words.childMeaning: Treating other people and their views with proper regard.
practiceSentences: Respectfulness costs nothing and is remembered.
What does respectfulness look like in a disagreement?
Respectfulness does not require agreement.
Her respectfulness towards every visitor set the tone.
Respectfulness is shown in how you listen, not only how you speak.

words.group: Word building: -ation, -ity and -ability
words.childMeaning: A complete and often surprising change in the form, appearance or nature of something.
practiceSentences: The transformation of the draft between March and June was total.
What transformation does the character undergo?
A transformation changes the nature of a thing, not only its surface.
Her transformation as a writer began with cutting adjectives.
In mathematics a transformation moves or resizes a shape.

words.group: Word building: -ation, -ity and -ability
words.childMeaning: The quality of being well founded and able to stand up to testing.
practiceSentences: The validity of the conclusion rests on one unchecked figure.
How would you test the validity of this argument?
Validity is about the reasoning; truth is about the world.
An argument can have validity and still reach a false conclusion.
A ticket has validity too, which is the everyday use of the word.

words.group: Word building: -ation, -ity and -ability
words.childMeaning: How much something varies from one measurement to the next.
practiceSentences: The variability between the two seasons made the average useless.
What variability would you expect in this data?
High variability hides a pattern that a mean pretends is there.
She reported the variability alongside the average, as she should.
Variability is how much it changes; a variable is what changes.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: The voice a poem is written in, which is not the poet.
practiceSentences: The speaker of the poem is a soldier, not the poet herself.
What do we learn about the speaker from the first line?
The speaker is a character the poet invents, sometimes unlike them entirely.
Confusing the speaker with the poet is the commonest mistake in essays.
Speaker also means anybody talking, which is why this use has to be taught.

words.group: Grammar: the two ways to describe a word's behaviour
words.childMeaning: To do with the words of a language rather than its grammar.
practiceSentences: The lexical choice between slim and skinny carries the whole judgement.
What lexical field does this poem draw on?
A lexical change alters which words are used, not how they are arranged.
She studied the lexical differences between the two translations.
Lexical is about vocabulary; syntactic is about structure.

words.group: Grammar: the two ways to describe a word's behaviour
words.childMeaning: To do with how words are arranged in a sentence.
practiceSentences: The syntactic structure changes where the emphasis falls.
What syntactic feature makes this sentence hard to read?
A syntactic error breaks the sentence; a lexical one only misnames.
The poet's syntactic inversions slow the reader deliberately.
Syntactic concerns arrangement; semantic concerns meaning.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: An official plan or set of rules that a school, company, or government follows.
practiceSentences: He said it was a necessary policy, not a punishment.
Who actually wrote this new policy, Sir?
Kian complained that the policy felt unfair to Form 3.
The board agreed to review the policy after hearing the students speak.
The library's new policy allows borrowing over the holidays.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: An official rule made to control how something is done.
practiceSentences: A regulation limits how deep a well may be dug.
Which regulation covers this case?
A regulation carries more force than a guideline.
New safety regulations came into effect in June.
Every regulation began as somebody's bad experience.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: The moment a seed begins to grow into a plant.
practiceSentences: Germination needs warmth, water and air.
How long does germination take for beans?
Light is not required for germination in most seeds.
The class recorded the germination of each seed.
No germination means no crop.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: Protected against a particular disease.
practiceSentences: The vaccine made her immune to the illness.
Are you immune after having it once?
The immune system fights germs day and night.
Nobody is immune to every disease.
Being immune is not the same as being careful.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: How plants make food from sunlight, water and air.
practiceSentences: Photosynthesis happens mostly in the leaves.
What does photosynthesis produce besides food?
Without photosynthesis there would be no oxygen.
Photosynthesis stops in the dark.
She explained photosynthesis using one leaf.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: How a living thing releases energy from its food.
practiceSentences: Respiration happens in every living cell.
How does respiration differ from breathing?
Respiration uses oxygen and releases energy.
Plants carry out respiration as well as photosynthesis.
Respiration continues while you sleep.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: To get or gain something, usually by effort or learning.
practiceSentences: The robotics club worked all term to acquire the parts needed for the championship build.
Which digital skills should students acquire before they leave secondary school?
"You will acquire speed with practice," the coding mentor promised, "so focus on accuracy first."
I hope to acquire enough editing experience this year to run the school's video channel myself.
They decided to acquire basic coding skills and build a simple weather-monitoring app.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: A difficult task that tests your ability or effort to overcome it.
practiceSentences: Every growing city faces the same challenge: too many people and not enough roads.
Is fixing the traffic the biggest challenge facing Mogadishu right now?
Nadir called it an exciting challenge rather than a problem to complain about!
The students accepted the challenge of designing a better bus-route map.
Two weeks before the school's Independence Day event, Jamal faced another challenge.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: To ask about something to get information.
practiceSentences: If one step confuses you, enquire before you carry on with the rest.
Nora went to the school office to enquire about the missing library book.
Shall we enquire at the community centre about the times for the fair?
'I would like to enquire about the science competition,' said Kian politely.
Yesterday I enquired at the bookshop whether the new comics had arrived.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: To suggest an explanation that can then be tested.
practiceSentences: We hypothesise that the shorter route is also the slower one.
What would you hypothesise from these readings?
To hypothesise is to propose something you intend to test.
She hypothesised a cause and designed an experiment for it.
If you cannot test what you hypothesise, it is only an opinion.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: To show or point out something.
practiceSentences: The survey results indicate that most teenagers now receive their news through short videos.
What do the falling subscription numbers indicate about the future of printed newspapers?
'These figures indicate a serious problem,' said the analyst, pointing at the audience graph.
My battery statistics indicate that I spend far longer on games than I ever admit.
Dark clouds over the sea usually indicate rain by evening.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: To decide which things matter most and do them first.
practiceSentences: Prioritise the tasks that everything else depends on.
How would you prioritise these five jobs?
To prioritise is to choose what to leave until later.
She prioritised the repairs over the decoration.
Prioritising means something only if something is dropped.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: To make two people or groups friendly again after a disagreement.
practiceSentences: The shared harvest meal gave the two feuding neighbours a graceful chance to reconcile at last.
Why do festivals so often inspire relatives to reconcile after years of stubborn silence?
"Let us reconcile before the celebration," wrote Uncle, "because joy tastes better without bitterness."
I believe the courage to reconcile first is a greater gift than anything wrapped in paper.
Imani also helped reconcile students who had quarrelled.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: To make something stronger, or to support a point with more evidence.
practiceSentences: Steel rods reinforce the concrete beam.
What evidence would reinforce this argument?
A second source reinforces the first, or it contradicts it.
She reinforced the corners of the box with tape.
To reinforce is to add strength to what is already there.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: To stand for something, or to act on behalf of a person or group.
practiceSentences: Each of you will represent a group at the final debate.
Who will represent the fishermen at the discussion?
A single juror cannot represent every opinion in the room.
On this map, one centimetre represents a whole kilometre.
To represent is to stand for something, or to stand in for somebody.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: To form an idea that explains a set of facts.
practiceSentences: Historians theorise about why the settlement was abandoned.
What would you theorise from this evidence?
To theorise before gathering evidence is to guess.
She theorised that the two events were connected.
To theorise is to explain many facts; to hypothesise is to test one.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: To add notes to a text explaining or commenting on it.
practiceSentences: Annotate the passage before you write about it.
How would you annotate this diagram?
To annotate is to think on the page.
She annotated every source in the margin.
Annotate the argument, not just the difficult words.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: Going up, or arranged from smallest to largest.
practiceSentences: Put the measurements in ascending order.
Which list is in ascending order?
Ascending order starts with the smallest value.
The path was ascending steadily for an hour.
Ascending goes up; descending goes down.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: Going down, or arranged from largest to smallest.
practiceSentences: Sort the results in descending order of size.
Is this table ascending or descending?
Descending order puts the largest value first.
The aeroplane was descending towards the coast.
Descending starts at the top and works down.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: The number placed in front of a letter in algebra.
practiceSentences: In 5x the coefficient is five.
What is the coefficient of y here?
A coefficient multiplies the letter it stands before.
She collected the terms and added their coefficients.
A coefficient of one is usually not written at all.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: A rule written in symbols showing how quantities relate.
practiceSentences: The formula for the area of a rectangle is length times width.
Which formula would you use here?
A formula works for every case, not just this one.
She substituted the numbers into the formula.
The plural of formula is formulae, or formulas.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: Describing a fraction whose top number is the larger one.
practiceSentences: Seven quarters is an improper fraction.
Is this fraction improper or proper?
An improper fraction is worth one or more.
Convert the improper fraction to a mixed number.
Improper also means not suitable or not correct.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: The opposite operation, which undoes the first one.
practiceSentences: Subtraction is the inverse of addition.
What is the inverse of multiplying by four?
An inverse operation returns you to where you started.
She checked her answer using the inverse.
In an inverse relationship, one rises as the other falls.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: Combined two or more different things together.
practiceSentences: The field was the only open space nearby, a place where joy and rivalry mixed like dust and sweat.
Why had joy and rivalry mixed so easily on that dusty football field?
What strange feelings mixed together inside Jamal as he walked away that day!
Excitement and nerves mixed inside Alina as she read her mother's old letters.
The article mixed opinion and fact with no clear introduction or logical organisation.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: Making a shape larger or smaller while keeping its proportions.
practiceSentences: A dilation changes the size and not the shape.
What scale factor does this dilation use?
After a dilation the two shapes are similar, not congruent.
She drew the dilation from a centre point on the grid.
Dilation also means the widening of the pupil in an eye.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: The result of something, or one possible result in probability.
practiceSentences: Rolling a six is one outcome out of six.
What outcome did the experiment produce?
Every outcome of a fair die is equally likely.
The outcome surprised everybody except the youngest.
An outcome is what happened; an aim is what was wanted.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: Able to work or exist together without conflict.
practiceSentences: The new printer is compatible with every machine in the room.
Are these two accounts compatible?
Two compatible claims can both be true at once.
She looked for a compatible file format.
Compatible means they fit together, not that they are the same.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: Stiff and not able to bend, or unwilling to change.
practiceSentences: A rigid frame does not flex under load.
Is the rule rigid, or is there room to judge?
A rigid plan breaks where a flexible one bends.
The card was rigid enough to stand upright.
Rigid describes a material, and also an attitude.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: Better than something else, or higher in rank.
practiceSentences: The second design proved superior in every test.
Which method is superior for this task?
A superior result deserves an explanation, not just applause.
She reported the fault to her superior.
Superior means better than something named, so name it.

words.group: Words: bringing the year together
words.childMeaning: The freedom to make your own decisions.
practiceSentences: The club was given autonomy over its own budget.
How much autonomy should a class have?
Autonomy brings responsibility with it, always.
Their autonomy ended where the school's rules began.
Autonomy is self-government, whether of a person or a region.
